summary: Proposal card shows a single change the agent wants to make, like a new colour for a low-contrast button, as a before and after with the agent's confidence. The person can accept the suggestion, pick one of the other options instead, or say not now, and either choice can be undone.
use: When the agent spots a fix during a review and should ask before applying it.
When there is more than one reasonable fix and the agent should rank them.
When people need to see how sure the agent is before they accept.
When an accepted or dismissed suggestion should be easy to take back.
features: The current value (`from`) and the chosen option sit side by side as swatches with a label and an optional badge, such as a contrast ratio.
A five-segment meter and a percentage show the chosen option's `confidence`. It fills in shortly after the card appears and follows each new pick.
The first entry in `options` is the agent's pick. The others sit behind an "N other options" toggle, and clicking one makes it the change.
Accept calls `onAccept` with the chosen option and its index, closes the options list and shows `acceptedLabel`.
Not now shows `dismissedLabel`. Both end states offer Undo, which reopens the card and calls `onUndo`.
Badge tones default to bad for the current value and ok for the options, and can be set per value with `tone`.
a11y: The confidence bar has `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow` and an `aria-label`.
The other-options toggle is a button with `aria-expanded`.
When the options list is closed it is `inert` and `aria-hidden`.
With reduced motion turned on, the confidence count jumps straight to its value.

faq.q: Which option is the agent's suggestion?
faq.a: The first one in `options`. `defaultValue` is 0, so it shows as the change until the person picks another.

faq.q: How do I apply the change when someone accepts it?
faq.a: Handle `onAccept(option, index)`. The card only records the decision, so applying and reverting the change happens in your code, with `onUndo` for the revert.

faq.q: Can I use it for something other than colours?
faq.a: Each value has a `color` for its swatch and a free-text `label` and `badge`, so it fits any change that can be shown as a swatch and a short value.
